insights.topic: Verified purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol has generated 7,180 cryptographically verified purchase receipts — deterministic proof of transaction, not inferred intent. Every major cookieless alternative still operates on inference; this is the structural gap.

Verified receipt settlement runs at ~$0.10 per confirmed purchase event (148 sats); ad tech CPA for probabilistic attribution runs $5–$150. That's a 50–200x cost differential grounded in actual settlement data, not modeled projections.

insights.topic: Brand universe now spans full retail stack
insights.insight: Top brands in the 14-day window include Walmart, Amazon, Dollar General, Depop, and Best Buy — physical big-box, online marketplace, discount, and peer-to-peer resale in the same verified dataset. No single targeting platform currently covers this range with purchase confirmation.

insights.topic: Digital commerce receipts are now a primary signal vector
insights.insight: DKIM-verified purchase confirmation emails from Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Suno confirm the dataset captures SaaS, AI products, and creator economy transactions alongside physical retail — a cross-spectrum purchase graph that ad tech cannot replicate from browser signals alone.

insights.topic: Geographic reach now includes non-metro and lower-income segments
insights.insight: Three consecutive heartbeats above 68% CBSA diffusion rate, plus Dollar General's entry into the top brand list, indicate the network has extended beyond urban early adopters into rural and lower-income consumer segments — segments historically underrepresented in premium data products.

The 7-day GMV window moved from $24K to $52K in roughly 72 hours; the underlying receipt volume is compounding even as single-week velocity remains below prior-period baseline. The dataset is growing faster than the headline velocity figure suggests.
